summary: Activision's military shooter series, covering the World War II originals, Modern Warfare, Black Ops, console side games, remasters, and live-service Warzone/Mobile releases.

entries.title: Call of Duty

primary.why: The first game was built for PC, and Windows remains the most configurable complete route; Call of Duty Classic is an HD console access route but not the preferred main version.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows release with compatibility/widescreen fixes, then United Offensive separately for the expansion campaign.

secondary.why: The N-Gage release is a separate adaptation rather than the PC original.

entries.remaster_caveats: Call of Duty Classic is a console port, not the preferred main route.

primary.why: United Offensive is the expansion to the original Call of Duty and is best preserved on Windows with the base game.
primary.how_to_play: Install after Call of Duty on Windows and apply compatibility fixes before capture.

entries.title: Call of Duty: Finest Hour

emulation.notes: Use Xbox emulation or original hardware.

primary.why: Finest Hour is a console-only side game; Xbox is the highest-fidelity route among its releases.
primary.how_to_play: Play on Xbox hardware or xemu; use PS2/GameCube only for comparison.

entries.remaster_caveats: Console-only side game, not a port of the PC original.

primary.why: Windows is the highest-fidelity and most configurable route for Infinity Ward's sequel.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows release with compatibility/widescreen fixes; treat Big Red One as a separate side game.

entries.title: Call of Duty 2: Big Red One

emulation.notes: Use Xbox emulation or original hardware.

primary.why: Big Red One is a separate console campaign, and Xbox is the strongest route.
primary.how_to_play: Play on Xbox hardware or xemu.

entries.remaster_caveats: Separate from Call of Duty 2, not a direct port.

primary.why: Call of Duty 3 never released on PC, so Xbox 360 is the best high-fidelity official route.
primary.how_to_play: Play on Xbox 360 hardware or a verified Xenia setup; use PS3/Wii/PS2/Xbox only for comparison.

entries.title: Call of Duty: Roads to Victory

primary.why: Roads to Victory is PSP-only, and PPSSPP gives the best fidelity route.
primary.how_to_play: Play the PSP release in PPSSPP at high internal resolution.

entries.title: Call of Duty 4: Modern Warfare

primary.why: Modern Warfare Remastered is the highest-fidelity route for the campaign/core content, while the original PC build still matters for original multiplayer/mod context.
primary.how_to_play: Play Modern Warfare Remastered on Windows for the main route; preserve the 2007 PC original separately for historical multiplayer/mods.

secondary.why: It is a distinct port, not the best main route.

secondary.what_to_play: Archive as its own handheld version.
secondary.why: It is a different game build.

entries.remaster_caveats: Original multiplayer/mod history is not fully replaceable by the remaster.

entries.title: Call of Duty: World at War

primary.why: Windows is the highest-fidelity complete route for Treyarch's World War II entry and original Zombies debut.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows release with patches/DLC where available; archive Final Fronts and DS separately.

entries.title: Call of Duty: World at War - Final Fronts

primary.why: Final Fronts is a PS2-only side game with a different campaign, so PCSX2 is the best route.
primary.how_to_play: Play in PCSX2 at high internal resolution.

entries.remaster_caveats: Separate from the main World at War release.

emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Windows PC original; campaign remaster for campaign visuals

primary.why: The 2020 remaster covers only the campaign, so the original Windows release remains the most complete full-game route for campaign, Special Ops, multiplayer, and DLC.
primary.how_to_play: Play the original Windows release for the full package; play Campaign Remastered separately only for higher-fidelity campaign capture.

secondary.exclusive_content: Modern Warfare 2 Campaign Remastered provides a visually upgraded campaign-only route.
secondary.what_to_play: Replay campaign only if high-fidelity campaign capture matters.
secondary.why: The remaster lacks the full original multiplayer/Special Ops package.

primary.why: Windows is the highest-fidelity complete route for the first Black Ops game.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows release with DLC/patches where available; archive DS/mobile Zombies separately.

entries.title: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 3

primary.why: Windows is the highest-fidelity complete route for the 2011 Modern Warfare trilogy finale.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows release with DLC/patches; do not conflate with the 2023 Modern Warfare III reboot-sequel.

entries.remaster_caveats: No remaster; distinct from 2023 Modern Warfare III.

entries.title: Call of Duty: Black Ops II

primary.why: Windows is the highest-fidelity complete route for Black Ops II.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows release with DLC/patches; use Wii U only for platform comparison.

entries.title: Call of Duty: Black Ops: Declassified

primary.why: Declassified is Vita-only, making Vita hardware the official route.
primary.how_to_play: Play on PlayStation Vita hardware; Vita3K is only a preservation test route after compatibility verification.

primary.why: Call of Duty Online was a regional Windows free-to-play service and is now defunct, so it is a preservation/shutdown entry.
primary.how_to_play: No official live route remains; archive only with verified client/server preservation.

primary.why: Strike Team was a mobile-only tactical shooter; Android is the more flexible archival route.
primary.how_to_play: Use a documented Android app build; iOS is equivalent for normal historical play.

primary.why: Windows is the highest-fidelity route for Ghosts and supports the full cross-gen content/DLC package.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows release with DLC/patches; use current-generation console versions only for comparison.

primary.why: Windows is the highest-fidelity route, and the PC/current-gen versions are the best way to play the full Advanced Warfare package.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows release with DLC/patches; avoid last-gen versions for main capture.

emulation.notes: Only useful with preserved app/service support.

primary.why: Heroes was a mobile strategy game and is now defunct, so Android is the most flexible preservation route if a build is available.
primary.how_to_play: No official live route remains; document app/server state and preserved builds only.

entries.title: Call of Duty: Black Ops III

primary.version: Zombies Chronicles / PC release with DLC
primary.why: Windows is highest fidelity and the full-feature route; seventh-generation console versions lack the campaign.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows release with Zombies Chronicles and DLC where desired; avoid PS3/Xbox 360 for main play.

entries.title: Call of Duty: Infinite Warfare

primary.why: Windows is the highest-fidelity route; special editions bundled Modern Warfare Remastered but Infinite Warfare itself is best on PC.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows release with DLC/patches; archive Modern Warfare Remastered separately.

entries.remaster_caveats: Special editions bundled Modern Warfare Remastered, which has its own entry.

entries.title: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare Remastered

primary.why: The remaster is visually definitive for the Modern Warfare campaign/core content, and Windows is the most configurable platform.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows release; use the 2007 PC original for original multiplayer/mod preservation.

entries.remaster_caveats: Initially bundled with Infinite Warfare special editions before standalone release.

primary.why: Windows is the highest-fidelity route for Sledgehammer's World War II entry.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows release with DLC/patches.

primary.why: Black Ops 4 has no traditional campaign and is best on Windows for fidelity/settings across multiplayer, Zombies, and Blackout.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows release; document server/service state because the game is online-focused.

entries.title: Call of Duty: Mobile

emulation.notes: Use with documented app version and control setup.

primary.why: Mobile is Android/iOS only, and Android is the most flexible route for versioned preservation and emulator testing.
primary.how_to_play: Play the current Android build or preserve a documented app version; record season/content state.

entries.remaster_caveats: Live mobile service; archive by app version/season.

entries.title: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare

primary.why: The 2019 reboot is best on Windows for fidelity/settings and is distinct from the 2007 original.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows release; document install components, Warzone integration history, and current service state.

entries.remaster_caveats: Reboot; do not conflate with Call of Duty 4: Modern Warfare.

primary.why: The original Warzone was a Windows/PS4/Xbox One free-to-play release and is now defunct, so Windows is the best archival route if a preserved build/service exists.
primary.how_to_play: No official live route remains; record map/season/client history and use Warzone 2022 for current play.

entries.title: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 2 Campaign Remastered

primary.why: This remaster is visually definitive for the Modern Warfare 2 campaign but does not replace the original full game.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows remaster for campaign visuals only; use original MW2 for the full package.

entries.remaster_caveats: Campaign only; no original multiplayer or Special Ops.

entries.title: Call of Duty: Black Ops Cold War

primary.why: Windows is the highest-fidelity route for the cross-gen Black Ops Cold War package.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows build; document installed mode packs and service state.

primary.why: Windows is the highest-fidelity route for Vanguard's cross-gen package.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows build; document installed modes and service state.

entries.title: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare II

primary.why: The 2022 reboot-sequel is best on Windows for fidelity/settings and is distinct from the 2009 Modern Warfare 2.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows build; document Call of Duty HQ/install component state.

entries.remaster_caveats: Reboot-sequel; do not conflate with the 2009 game.

entries.title: Call of Duty: Warzone

primary.why: The current Warzone service is best on Windows for fidelity/settings and capture.
primary.how_to_play: Play the current Windows build through Call of Duty HQ; record season/map/install state.

entries.remaster_caveats: Separate current service from the defunct 2020 Warzone service.

entries.title: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare III

primary.why: The 2023 reboot-sequel is best on Windows for fidelity/settings and is distinct from the 2011 Modern Warfare 3.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows build; document Call of Duty HQ/install component state.

entries.remaster_caveats: Reboot-sequel; do not conflate with the 2011 game.

emulation.notes: Only useful with preserved app/service support.

primary.why: Warzone Mobile released on Android/iOS and is now defunct, making Android the more flexible archival route if a verified build exists.
primary.how_to_play: No official live route remains; document app version, shutdown state, and preserved builds only.

primary.why: Windows is the highest-fidelity route for Black Ops 6, with current-gen and last-gen console versions available.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows build; document Game Pass/Call of Duty HQ/install state and current season content.

entries.title: Call of Duty: Black Ops 7

primary.why: Black Ops 7 is the latest shipped Call of Duty as of June 16, 2026; Windows is the highest-fidelity/settings route across Steam, Battle.net, Xbox PC, and Game Pass.
primary.how_to_play: Play the current Windows build; document season, edition, and Call of Duty HQ install state.

entries.remaster_caveats: Latest live entry; record season/patch state.
